html:
Zanabazar was the first Bogd Gegeen, the highest Buddhist leader of the Khalkha Mongols, and one of the finest artists Mongolia has produced.

He was a son of the Tüsheet Khan, one of the leading Khalkha princes. In 1639, at four years old, he was declared the Khalkha's spiritual leader. He studied in Tibet, and the 5th Dalai Lama recognised him as a reincarnation of a famous scholar. He founded monasteries and spread the Gelug school in Mongolia.

He cast graceful gilt bronze statues of Buddhas and the goddess Tara, still prized today, and in 1686 he created the Soyombo script, whose symbol is now on Mongolia's flag.

When the Dzungars invaded Khalkha in 1688, he led the Khalkha to seek the protection of the Kangxi Emperor of the Qing, a choice that bound Mongolia to China until 1911. His line of reincarnations ended with the Bogd Khan.
